text_fidelity_a: Etekcity Camping Air Mattress Inflatable Single High Airbed Blow up Bed Tent Mattress with Rechargeable Air Pump, Height 9", Carry Bag I have been through 4 air mattresses and each one sucked, so I was not expecting much from this one. I didn't even want to try another one, but to get my partner to agree to go camping I had to supply an air mattress so I went with the one with the highest rating within my budget and waited to be disappointed. Imagine my surprise. You can charge the pump from your vehicle (no batteries! which was great because they didn't even cross my mind) or from a regular outlet. The pump is noisy but not unusually so, and the mattress inflated pretty darn quick. It was ample for 2 large people and 2 small dogs. Best of all, incredibly, it didn't deflate overnight! I did "top it off" a bit for the 3rd night but over-all it was full and comfy, survived excited dogs and 40 degree weather, the pump has a reverse so you can deflate it really fast, and somehow, someway, it actually all fit back easily into the box it came in so we can keep it safe for next time. It wasn't even overpoweringly stinky like plastic usually is (we still aired it out of course, how stinky is too stinky being quite subjective but neither of us was bothered).  If someone asked me to recommend an air mattress, I would gleefully direct them to this one.

text_fidelity_a:
Timex Personal Trainer Heart Rate Monitor Watch - Gray I had purchased this as a Christmas gift, but my wife thought she might be allergic to the chest strap. So I am using it. The watch and chest strap are well made. Here are some things you should know:

1. you must use the chest strap. You get no heart/pulse rate readings on the watch without it. The chest strap is easy on, easy off.
2. once you affix the chest strap, you will forget you have it on.
3. you need to wet a portion of the chest strap before applying it for the day. I simply put a swipe of water on each part of the strap on either side of the Timex logo. You only need do this once per day, or so I have found.
4. while you can change the battery in the chest strap yourself, the manual recommends a professional change the watch battery.
5. the manual itself requires some close attention if you are to get the full benefit of the monitor. I am still figuring out all of the bells and whistles.
6. the recorded HR on this watch matches the treadmill HR monitor at the gym as well as our BP machine.

When I read that other reviewers bought this item based on their heart doctor's suggestion, I thought that was good enough for me. My wife's loss is my gain (smile)!

UPDATE, March 14,2013
I continue to enjoy the use of this product immensely. Note that when you are not using the HR monitor feature, it serves as a timepiece. And finally, a note to those who, like me, are hearing impaired. On the first day I used this monitor, I went to see my hearing aid dispenser for a check-up. He immediately said, "What's beeping?" I said, is it my phone? He said no, it seems to be coming from . . . there. He meant the monitor on my wrist! I myself could not hear it a lick! So: if you see a tiny chime icon on the watch face in monitor mode, then anyone close to you can hear what I surmise are rhythmic beeps. The chime feature can be turned off, as I discovered after I spent a half-day announcing my presence to the world!
text_fidelity_b: Timex Personal Trainer Heart Rate Monitor Watch - Gray

text_fidelity_a:
Myklops Rear View Mirror On the whole, I'm happy with my purchase and find it very useful when I'm riding. I've got a folding bike, which I love but limits my choice of mirrors. I tried different ones that attach to glasses or helmets, but I could never find one that quite fit; besides, I always worried they would drop off the moment I hit a bump. I figured the Myklops was my best option.

As others have noted, objects in this review are a heck of a lot closer than they appear. However, I've gotten used to this and find the mirror very helpful for spotting cars, trucks, and other larger vehicles in traffic. For spotting other bikes, skateboarders, and standing scooter riders (scooterists?), it's not as helpful. Being smaller, they're usually on me well before I pick them up in the mirror. Luckily, that's usually not a problem. With motorcycles and mopeds/scooters, it's a mixed bag. The bigger they are, they easier they are to pick out in the mirror. Usually it's the noise of their engines that I notice first, then I know to look for them in the mirror. So this mirror is helpful, but not as much as I'd like.

Sturdiness is hard to speak to without lots of time going by, but I've been using this regularly for over six weeks, tossing it into bags when I'm not riding with it, and it's holding up. I find the cover a little fiddly to close, but it does latch into place with a little patience. The biggest challenge was remembering to push the arms back into the base before taking by backpack off once I'd gotten to where I was going, but that's pilot error on my part. I don't yank at the arms or twist them hard, but neither am I super delicate with them. They feel the same as they did out of the package, so I'm hopeful that they'll last a while.

As for stability, I find the mirror to be very stable once I've extended the arms and positioned it how I like. The band sometimes shifts around my wrist as I ride, but I don't think this is a fault of the product. I usually wear long-sleeved shirts, the material of which is often a bit loose, so I need to be more careful about smoothing that down and not letting it bunch before fastening the strap. When I'm wearing shorter sleeves with tighter fitting sun gloves, the band stays in place. Also, I'm very pleased that the velcro on the band is on the gentle side. By that I mean that it doesn't have large teeth of the sort that often damage my clothes. Despite being careful, I sometimes catch my clothing on it, but so far (touch wood) it hasn't caused any pilling or tearing of the fabric ... and these are fairly delicate materials I'm talking about, so that's a major bonus.

I think it's impossible to make a perfect mirror that fits all my riding needs. But this comes pretty darn close. Funnily enough, as I sat down to write this review, I noticed that there's currently a nice little discount for it, no doubt for Black Friday/Cyber Monday/or other seasonal sales holiday here. I paid full price for mine, but I'm okay with that. At full price, I feel like I got my money's worth, and I would definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: Myklops Rear View Mirror

Joby Gorillatorch Blade Tactical Flashlight I was highly impressed with this flashlight. It is a nice, clean design, and the adjustable tripod allows you to put the light right where you need it, especially in tight places such as in the interior of a computer. The rear switch is perfect for carrying the light in your fist and working with your thumb. A real plus: it has flat sides so when you put it down it does not roll away!

The light itself is very bright (I almost want to advise "Do not look into light with remaining eyeball"), especially on the highest setting. You can adjust the aperture for a wide or a narrow beam. We have inadequate lighting in our back yard, which extends back at least 15 yards (probably more), and using this flashlight in almost total darkness I could see the details of the trees and back fence while walking our dog.

USB charging is very convenient, since it is now such a universal technology. When plugged in to charge, the unit glows blue until done, so it's very easy to know when its finished. This is an excellent piece of equipment for use in an emergency kit or just for plain everyday use.

Downsides: the rear cover over the charging port and the switch seem flimsy, and there's no way to change out the battery that I can find (nor is it mentioned in the manual). However, I would still highly recommend this product.

Because I won't be sharing this with anyone else, I cut some of the extra length off, but if you're sharing with someone tall, you might not want to do that.

The counter issue that several people have mentioned concerned me at first, too, but then I read that you MUST have the counter in your right hand. If you don't, the rope will be turning in the wrong direction so of course it's not going to count. Once I made sure the counter was in my right hand, I found the counter to be accurate and reliable.

I would have given this five stars, but five stars means "I love it" and I can't say I love it. This is not because the product doesn't deserve the high rating; it's because I find I really don't love jumping rope with a lighter weight jump rope. I loved it when I was a kid and we were literally jumping ropes on the playground with those heavy ropes that thwacked when they hit the ground and gave a pleasurable sensation on the upswing. There's no way to make a lightweight jump rope that has that kind of tactile feedback, and that's what I always loved about jumping rope.

Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) FitBit Charge 2 HeartRate and Fitness Wristband.
Update: I have been using this watch for 6 months.
Pros-
App-I have used the mobile app and the program on the computer to use the product. The app is very nice, user friendly.
HeartRate Function-I like the heart rate function. Just knowing my heart rate at various times of the day and night, and while working out is important to me.
Multi-Sport Tracking-I like choosing which exercise I am going to do on the watch.
Cons- The watch does not keep track of how many miles I bike ride when using the exercise bike. The watch only records the amount of time I am on the bike. Then it transfers a number to amount of floors I have climbed instead of miles on the bike.
Smart Watch Notification- I have to be near my mobile device for the notification to work.
Band is Too Wide-I do not like the size of the band. The band is too wide for my preference.
Size of Watch. I had to return the first watch I purchased. I had choosen the large size and it was too big. My wrist is 6 inches, thats 15cm. The size small is still too big for my wrist. Their are 10 notches in the watch to adjust it to for length. I wear mine 6 notches from the top!
Watch Not Comfortable to sleep with. The band is too large to be comfortable to sleep with.

Pure Pulse Heart Rate-The FitBit Charge 2 has a continous heart rate. It is really nice to be able to monitor heart rate while working out, especially when using the treadmill.
All day Activity-The watch tracks your activity all day (including amount of steps, floors climbed, interval training, treadmill, weights, workout, elliptical, running, bike, heart monitor, and calories burned). The activity can be transferred to the app.
Sleep-The watch tracks your sleep. After you sleep you can transfer the information to the app to view how well you slept. It shows how many times you woke up, how many times you were restless.
Multi-Sport Tracking-You choose on your watch what workout you will do. The watch tracks your progress and heart rate. After exercising transfer the information to the app. You can see all of the information including graphs of heart rate, intensity of workout. The choices are treadmill, weights, workout, elliptical, running, and bike.
Smartphone Notifications, and Interchangeable Bands. Their are different choices for the watch band and they are available for purchase separately.
Size-Compair between Small and Large. The difference between the Small and the Large is the length of the wristband. The length of the small band is 5.5-6.9 inch (13.9cm- 17.5 cm). The length of the large is 6.3-8.2 inch (16.0-20.8).
The app- You can Run the app using a mobile device or a computer. With the computer you use a web site instead of an app. The site is FitBit.com The FitBit Dashboard is available on the app or on the computer. View on the dashboard: steps, calories burned, floors, active minutes, sleep, weight goals, calories burned, cups to drink, vibrate alarm, clock faces, and graphs. The graphs are: calorie intake and burn, steps, distance, floors, time active, sleep, and weight. Connect with friends to inspire and compete in challenges, weight goals and food logging, and celebrate milestones with badges. I like how I can made changes and adjustments in the app. For example for Interval workout I can choose the time for working out and resting. Easy to Read Clock Face-Choose from several clock faces displaying stats. The clock face is black and white. For example one of the clock faces to choose from displays time, date, steps and continous heart rate.
Water-Resistance and works with Aria Wi-Fi Smart Scale
Works with IOS, Android and Windows devices, Mac and PC.

But this one appeared to have some advantages the others didn't. There wasn't any instructions on using this cane, but it wasn't too hard to figure out. To adjust the length there are three sections which can be pulled out to make the cane longer. The cane in it's fully collapsed state is 21" long, fully extended its 42". To change the lengths you twist the shafts which loosen or tighten the assembly depending on the direction you twist. You can actually pull out a section completely if you're not careful (it slips back in pretty easily). The tip of the cane is interesting. There is a rubber foot that can be removed which exposes a small diameter metal point, that I assume is for use on icy surfaces (we don't get that too often here in Texas). There is another thing that can be screwed on the end of the cane, some sort of round dome looking thing, I haven't a clue what it's purpose might be.

Over-all I happy with the walking stick, I like that it collapses down like it does for easy storage & carrying. And that it feels like pretty solid support when in use. I'm happy with my purchase.

SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black There is a major difference between this tube and its non thorn-resistant counterparts. The difference translates to a 3x larger package and a 3x stiffer inner tube. Whether this means that it will intercede on your behalf when penetrating objects attempt to derail your day, time will tell. But I can tell you that:

1) It takes some effort to stuff this piece of salami into your tire. It doesn't bend willingly.
2) It takes some getting used to on the road. Your tire will absorb less shock from road imperfections, resulting in a harsh ride. It's not like riding on solid rubber, but it's not as soft as a regular inner tube.

In my opinion, the harsh ride is worth it on a daily commuter, where reliability is paramount. I'm not sure if I'd use this on a recreational bike. A suspension bike may be fine.

Update: after a week or two, I stopped noticing the stiffer ride quality. Also, I have about 50lbs extra on that rear wheel, so my experience may not be typical (it's an e-bike).
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black

She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. text_fidelity_a:
OASMU Sand Free Beach Blanket Picnic Mat I live in an area about equidistant from the beach and the mountains. I like going to the beach but I much prefer the mountains, particularly in the autumn when the leaves change. One of the simple pleasures in life is having a picnic in the mountains, and this particular beach blanket is a good accessory for those trips.

This is not a blanket in the traditional sense. There is no padding, no fiber, no fringe. This is a very thin cover made of parachute nylon and it is very lightweight and thin. It will not provide any insulation from hard ground, nor will it provide much in the way of drying off after getting wet, but it is very water resistant and it will keep you from getting wet from wet ground unless you put it down on standing water.

Because this is such a lightweight blanket it means that it can be caught up with a good gust of wind. Provision has been made for that. There are pockets on the corners and they can be filled with sand at the beach or with stones when farther away. There are also loops on the corners for securing with pegs. Unfortunately there are no pegs included with this blanket and that is the one thing I would suggest for improvement.

I have a special use for this blanket. Along the Blue Ridge parkway there are picnic areas and my family and I like to go there for a nice picnic lunch. The blanket makes a perfect (although very large) tablecloth for the picnic table. When we’re done, it is very easy to clean and it packs up for the next trip with little effort.

I love the fact that this blanket compacts down to a size smaller than a football. It folds up very neatly and compactly and it fits in a pretty blue nylon bag with a pull tie. At that size it is small enough to fit in a shoulder bag or in just about any space in the car when traveling.

This is a very well-made blanket, too. I have found no issues with the stitching, the seams are straight and there are no nicks or cuts in the nylon material. I imagine that will change over years of use, but so far it still is pristine.

I am very happy with this beach blanket. It serves me well on picnics in the mountains, which is really all I could ask for. It is made well, it’s plenty large, and there are some thoughtful features that went into it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: OASMU Sand Free Beach Blanket Picnic Mat

Fizik Performance Bicycle Bar Tape - Soft, Tacky & Classic Professional Bike Handlebar Tape (2mm, 2.7mm, 3mm) This is a review of the updated Fizik Tempo Microtex Classic (2mm) bar tape. I have been using the old Fizik performance 3mm tacky bar tape on both my road and CX/gravel bikes for several years now, and while that tape was pretty difficult to install (especially on irregular bar shapes) I really liked the look and feel of it and the durability.

This 2mm Microtex tape was much easier to wrap my aero bars with compared to the thick and tacky version I have been using.. but I do prefer the feel of the thicker tacky tape. I can't really speak to the durability of this tape since I've only had it for a few rides but it seems durable when installing it and appears to be easy to clean.

Unfortunately it seems Fizik no longer makes perforated 3mm tacky tape, the new iterations are either flat unperforated tape or grooved channels. I'm not a big fan of the grooved look of the Vento tapes but I may consider using the flat Terra version when I need to rewrap my CX bike.. I really wish they would release a tacky version of the Tempo perforated tape though as I much prefer that look.

text_fidelity_a:
Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30 What a great reel for big, powerful fish! If you target fish that measure in the hundreds of pounds, and you want the best tool for the job, this is your reel. In my case, it's the reel I use when we go deep for big halibut here in Alaska. This reel holds plenty of line to get to those shelves 400 feet down where the barndoors lie, with plenty of line left over to allow for long runs that those big fish make. If you hang up and break off, losing several hundred feet of line (it happens), you don't have to hang it up because the reel holds enough line to let you keep fishing.

I like the high-speed retrieve for pulling up from the deep when you need to check your bait or try something else. When you latch into a fish, though, a quick push of the button on the hub of the handle engages the more powerful lower gears, so you can really torque into the fish.

That new handle design is nice, too. It comfortably fits my hand, has a nice rubbery, no-slip texture, and helps spread the stress across the meaty part of my hand so long battles are just a little bit easier.

The open design of the "X" series frame (with no crossbars across the front of the spool) is helpful when there's a backlash to deal with (yeah, it still happens once in a while). These reels aren't cheap, but they're the best you can buy. Solid, reliable, and made in USA. No regrets here!

Let me know if you don't anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30

TriggerPoint Grid Vibe Vibrating Foam Roller for Pain Relief, Relaxation, and Recovery When I first saw it, I thought, "It's so little, what am I going to do with that?" With the press of a button all of that changed…

Let's be honest: if you own a foam roller, a part of you enjoys pain. The trigger point roller is a nightmare of the heavenly sort. My muscles have never been so grateful!

My quads are pretty tight, and when foam rolling with the trigger point roller, it was like a deep tissue massage; the vibration makes a significant difference in the give of the muscles, in that it allows the roller to go deeper for the same amount of pain from a conventional roller. I also felt a huge relief when rolling my glutes: its small size allows it to get into those hard-to-reach muscles.

The trigger point roller doesn't have any give when putting your weight on it like other rollers, but the vibration helps counteract the stiffness of the product.

The only thing I encountered is that the button sometimes doesn't respond, and I have to keep pressing it until it works.

I give this little device five stars. Maybe the next one can be heated?…

Prorack 2-Bike Hitch Carrier I chose this bike rack before I realized what type of hitch it needed. I drive an old Honda Civic with no hitch at all. My husband has a hitch on his truck but it is the wrong kind. Today I went to a local U-Haul store and ordered the appropriate hitch to be installed on my car that would accept this bike rack. It will cost me $162.05 - this included the hitch and labor. So, I'm not able yet to review the bike rack itself, how nicely it will fit my new hitch, etc....but I certainly will when I get my hitch installed. I'm telling you this so that you will know not to get this bike rack if you don't have the square slide-in hitch installed on your vehicle.

On my way home from the U-haul store I was looking at cars and trucks to see if they had any hitches. I didn't see any hitches on regular sedans like my car, but I did see a few of the square hitches on trucks like Ford F150's, etc...

What I can say about the bike rack itself is that it is very heavy - it took both me and my husband to carry it from the door to the trunk of my car so I could take it to the hitch place. It seems to be sturdily constructed but I don't know how steadily it will hold our bikes until I can try it out next week when the hitch comes in. Believe me - I WILL update this review.

4.19.14 UPDATE

I have finally gotten around to actually putting this bike rack on my car using my new hitch. I was fairly painless by carefully following the enclosed directions. Me and my 12 year old daughter had it securely attached in about 30 minutes. We went sort of slow and I let her do a lot of the work so she could get some hands-on experience using basic tools. We put two children's sized bikes on it and found that the smaller the bike, the less stable it is, but they were secure enough for a trip to the park. You have to make sure that the tires are placed at the very ends of the long loop tire holders, but the the padded bars that come down over the frames were made for men's style bikes and the girl's style bike frames were held, but I could see that they were not as firmly gripped as they would be if the bike frame bars went straight across instead of sloping downwards. The bike rack sticks out about a foot and a half from the rear of the car so I have to be extra careful to make sure I'm all the way in the garage before letting the automatic garage door down.
text_fidelity_b: Prorack 2-Bike Hitch Carrier

I know it must sound silly to be so gushy about an umbrella, but I have never found a foldable umbrella that offered decent performance. This works just as well as my full-size umbrella with the huge benefit of being able to be folded up and carried in a briefcase.

The build quality is excellent, with well-made seams on the canopy, and very sturdy ribs. The automatic pop-up action is solid and quick to operate. The auto fold-up ability is equally well-done (e.g., you can push the “close” button and the canopy folds up, making it far easier to deal with once you’ve entered a building).

Wind resistance is quite good, with vent flaps that work well to prevent blowouts. The vents have a good amount of fabric overlap to keep any rain from getting through.

My only quibble is that it is hard to roll up so it fits back into the case. This canopy contains a lot of material and rolling/folding it up into a tight profile is a challenge. I didn’t have any problem folding it up enough to wrap it with the Velcro strap, but getting it to fit into the nylon pouch that it comes with is tough. I don’t consider that a negative since I never use those pouches, but point it out just in case that’s important to anyone who’s considering this.

Two huge (and dry) thumbs up for this umbrella. Great build quality, excellent performance, and compact when folded.

Topeak Adjustable Modula Cage EX Modified Shape Bicycle Waterbottle Cage Updated 6/18/14 - As predicted the plastic did break. While riding on a slightly bumpy road with a half filled bottle in the cage, the two plastic areas at the mount points simply gave way. The fix is fairly simple but may require a quick trip to a hardware store. Using rubber washers against the plastic and metal washers against the frame (mount points) and bolt heads, the cage is now [probably] better than new. I doubt it will break again, as the new mounting method distributes weight/load more evenly across the plastic, and the rubber washers offer a bit of shock-resistance. Hopefully the manufacturer will read this, having likely heard similar reports from other customers, and fix the issue - if not done already. I still like the design and flexibility.

Original Review: The only problem here is the plastic to metal nut that tightens down to hold the sliding cage in place. I do not see that lasting for a long time. But with a trip to the hardware store I was able to get all metal parts, with washers to protect the plastic cage, hoping to avoids cracks and snaps down the road. If you only use one size container, thus unlikely to move it around, the this should work just fine.
The great thing is that this does hold nearly any bottle within the size range in place, without issue. Even when mountain biking I had no problems with the 12oz Poland Springs bottle that was in there.

text_fidelity_a: Thule T2 Pro XT 2 Hitch Bike Rack (1.25"), Black We were so excited to get our new bike rack, but have been really disappointed. I followed all the guidelines and made sure this was the correct rack for my Subaru XV, and the right size for our dealer installed tow package.  First issue is that the safety latch doesn't fit right on the tow hitch. We were able to work around the issue and that hasn't been a problem.  We took the car on a 400 mile round trip road trip on highway and it did great.... the problem started last month. My husband got a new mountain bike with 29 in tires. We were driving maybe 5 miles from our house on a bumpy dirt road and despite being locked down really well, the bike bounced off and got dragged. He was NOT happy.  He thought maybe it was user error or he didn't do something right, and he went out again, this time putting his 27" tire bike on the back and making sure everything was locked down, but unfortunately the same thing happened on the super bumpy road. text_fidelity_a:
Westt Mountain Bike Helmet - Bicycle Helmets for Adults with LED Rear Light - Scooter MTB Skateboard Baseball Cycling Helmet Between her roller blades and our eScooters, my wife and I needed two new bike helmets. This was the one we got her and so far, we really like it. I normally do not talk about price points, but in this case: for the price point it feels, looks, and acts like a solid choice. We hope to never have to find out about the "protective" elements, but hope it holds up to that standard as well.

1. The Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light is a good looking helmet, so if looks are important, this has a nice look to it. We like the blue we picked and the overall look is cool.

2. The fit is good. My wife has a smaller head than mine, so we got one that was very adjustable - not really by choice in that we would have order one "size specific" if needed, but again, for her needs. In this case, the Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light allows you to adjust the size in a "one size fits all" situation. The dial on the back adjusts for you and so far it works well. She likes the fit she gets and feels comfortable between that adjustment and the strap.

3. There is no way to "test" this helmet without falling - and we are not test dummies - so we must trust this will have the good if ever needed. She took a good spill once off a SEGWAY and had a helmet on - which truly saved her - and so we swear by wearing head gear. Here I jump to the idea of "You get what you pay for." The helmet we were able to get for me was a far higher price (here on Amazon, over $200), and you CAN tell a difference. BUT, that said, compared to our previous, similarly priced helmets, this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light does seem to have what we need. Would we upgrade? Sure, who wouldn't? BUT, if price is a concern, and for most of us it is, would this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light do the trick? WE THINK SO. Again, there is NO way to know until you need it. BUT this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light fits like the ones we have had in the past and has a similar feel, so we are "trusting" it to take care of her if ever needed.

4. The inside lining IS thinner than mine. There is a difference in that kind of thing - bringing us back to, if we had the money we WOULD upgrade. But for what it is, this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light feels good on her head and she is comfortable.

5. The lights on the back are a huge bonus and work really well. There are (I think) 3 settings for different flashing options and we love that she can do this to bring attention to herself. That said, we have no intention of being out at night, but even in the daylight, it IS something that catches your eye.

In the end and overall we are very pleased with this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light and are happy to have it. Does price matter? You tell me. Yes, there IS a difference for a MUCH higher price point. But if the idea is to get something good on your head to keep you. safe, we think this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light offers us a great option.
text_fidelity_b: Westt Mountain Bike Helmet - Bicycle Helmets for Adults with LED Rear Light - Scooter MTB Skateboard Baseball Cycling Helmet

text_fidelity_a:
Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle I've had this bike a few months now. It is quiet (but not silent, there is a noise from the drive belt) but it is very smooth and responsive.

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

I will update the review if any issues with the bike itself come up. I love the bike, how smooth it runs, and the huge range of resistances available. It seems well-designed and like it will hold up. However, there are some big annoyances that will cost you extra $$$ to overcome.
text_fidelity_b: Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle

text_fidelity_a:
One Wheel Maya Cycle Bicycle Cargo Trailer Update: Trailer frame has rusted at the welds after just two exposures to rain. I live in the Sonora desert where humidity averages just 20% and it rarely rains. I will sell this trailer or donate it to a local coop.

Original Review [now edited]
I had to invest a few hours in prepping this trailer. If you are not mechanically adept you might need a bike shop to prep and attach this trailer but this could also be true with any trailer.

• The fragile plastic bushing where the trailer mates with the fork cracked and split on the very first use ($12+ shipping to replace it on the Maya website.) I made an addition purchase direct within weeks and asked Maya to replace the defective bushing. They merely ignored my request.
• 16” wheel axle arrived with bearings inadequately greased and cones not properly adjusted.
• Without the critical axle brackets and washers you’re out of business so you’ll want spares $19 + shipping)
• Light is visible through seams in the dry bag. Useless. I use a rigid storage tub instead.
• The dark red flag has no reflective quality making it completely useless for nighttime riding. I made an alternate from a neon yellow reflective vest
• Wing nuts are an invitation to tampering or theft. I used common 3/8 x 24 axle nuts with the built-in raised, scored washer
• Manual states: “an additional axle washer (not supplied) must be placed between the rear fork arm and the Maya axle adapters …” . Within 2 miles with the washers in place, the wheel would suddenly shift to jamb against the arm/stay so hard that the bike couldn’t be ridden. Luckily I had a slightly shorter axle

There was a tea candle. Yep.

Compass did not point North. Ever.

Glow sticks were not bright enough to illuminate the desk they were lying right on.

The fire starter is a joke. Don't get me wrong..With some skill it can be used, but it is absolute junk. I broke the metal bar after a few practice tries.

Overall, if I hadn't had a gift card to waste, I would have returned the item for a refund. Even my son who is all about zombie survival thought it was junk.

text_fidelity_a:
Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel I received this as a review sample and to be honest do not have any recent experience with air mattresses other than this one. That said, I did use it in my home for a solid week, both with the companion [[ASIN:B00U2VI1A8 Lightspeed Outdoors Foam Topper for Air Mattresses]] and without it. If that sounds odd, it's been a long time since I have slept in my bed. Long story, but I can attest that this is infinitely superior to the sofa on which I normally sleep.

Initially I slept on it for two days without the topper and it was absolutely comfortable. Part of that is I was able to stretch out more than I normally do because of the size. With the topper this is an entirely different piece of bedding. It's vastly more comfortable, but also introduces cleaning challenges. I would say that for occasional guests or short camping the topper merits consideration. For longer term use I am not so sure because the topper needs to be professionally cleaned periodically.

The included pump makes this a snap to fill. Note that you will need to supply four D batteries (I would have preferred eight of the more common AA ones, but that is a personal preference.) Deflating it was relatively easy, and it rolls and stores a lot easier than the topper that is made by the same company. In fact, this is lighter (to me, anyway) and less bulky than the topper, and takes up very little space in my home. It can easily store in the bottom drawer of my chest of drawers, or on a linen closet shelf. For camping this does not add a lot of weight when carrying it and a pack, which is another plus in my opinion.

Overall, this is far more comfortable than I remember old style air mattresses to be, and a lot easier to inflate, deflate and pack.

Performance Plus Carts Club Car DS Golf Cart Flip Folding Rear Back Seat Kit Diamond Plate - Off White I found that the packaging was a lot of the work when getting this project started. It seems they really focused on this as others mentioned issues with packaging.

The directions are better than most, but still not perfect. It does show you what to do but the explanations are missing depth. Overall I'd rate this as an intermediate level of expertise. A lot of that expertise is going to come from removing some of the equipment from the golf cart (versus the assembly of the seat to the golf cart).

I was not thrilled with the thinner material (I purchased a seat for a previous golf cart that had a bit thicker steel and the seats were a bit more durable). The seats do need self tapping screws to install into the thin diamond plate steel but it does look good. The handle that comes with the seat seems to provide structural support for the thinner steel rather than convenience. Though it does provide a more secure look to the cart.

IMPORTANT PART: The bigger issue I'm having now that it's all assembled is more and more cities are requiring rear seats to have seat belts. I had planned to install them as I did on my prior seat on my previous cart. That seat had bolt holes that seemed to plan for seat belts. This does not have holes for the belts and trying to find reasonable areas on the seat or cart aren't working. It seems like I'll be tapping some new holes to get those installed.

Outside of that I still did rate this well as it is a good looking seat once on the cart. The instructions are solid overall. The packaging was also done well (2 boxes too). I would recommend this to others.
text_fidelity_b: Performance Plus Carts Club Car DS Golf Cart Flip Folding Rear Back Seat Kit Diamond Plate - Off White

GSI Super Quality All-In-One Waterproof Heart Rate Monitor Watch and Transmitter Slim Chest Belt - For Exercise, Sports, Running, Jogging Outdoor Activities - Measures Speed, Pulse, Distance, Fat And Calories - Alarm And Stopwatch Functions I left the United States for 1 to 2 years in May, so I ordered TWO of these watches, one as a backup, because the predecessor died after about a year, and shipping to where I'm going is complicated (and super expensive!) at best!

Needless to say, after just a week, the first one fell off of my wrist while I was getting out of bed after some raucous activities (^_^) and fell about 3 feet (1 meter) to a carpeted hotel room. Imagine my surprise when I lifted it up and the display was dead (!!). I found a person in Bogota to replace the battery, but again, it died within less than 24 hours.

Sadly, I opened up my backup watch's case, less than a week into my 2 year journey. And after JUST FOUR DAYS, while I was walking the streets of Bogota, it started beeping beep beeping... and the screen got progressively dimmer. Until about a day later, it's screen was dead. I had the watch guy replace it, too, but it died within a week.

When I traveled to the Bahamas, I found a Garmin VivoSmart watch which does pretty much everything this does, and more, with an albeit worse interface, but it is wonderful so far and has lasted several months!
text_fidelity_b: GSI Super Quality All-In-One Waterproof Heart Rate Monitor Watch and Transmitter Slim Chest Belt - For Exercise, Sports, Running, Jogging Outdoor Activities - Measures Speed, Pulse, Distance, Fat And Calories - Alarm And Stopwatch Functions

The combination lock is unusual for a high-security bicycle lock and that part of the lock feels quite a bit lighter weight than our other locks. text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Talon 11 Men's Hiking Backpack , Cosmic Red, Small/Medium Rating is 4.5 stars, see below for why I took 0.5 stars off.

I recently used this backpack over about 10 days of hiking, much of it in hot weather up and down some mountain trails. I wanted comfort: firstly not making my back sticky and hot, and secondly being easy to wear loaded for 6 or more hours in a day. It passed both criteria with flying colors. There are bigger and smaller sizes, so you can get just what you need for your purposes, they should be just as comfortable.

The minor negatives I have are: (1) Ideally there would be a few more small compartments for things like wallets and phones and keys. It's easy to lose things in the depths when small items are packed in with fleece pullovers and jackets and granola bars and such. (2) It's pretty hard to reach back to grab and pull out your water bottles: I ended up working with my travel partner to help each other out for this. I'd prefer a way to set those just a bit forward, and put the little waist packs behind perhaps.

Overall I'm sold on Osprey backpacks, and would buy one again quite happily.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Talon 11 Men's Hiking Backpack , Cosmic Red, Small/Medium

text_fidelity_a:
FitDesk Desk Bike 3.0 - Folding Exercise Bike for Work from Home Fitness, Stationary Bike and Desk Exercise Equipment with Built-in Tablet Holder, Bike Desk Workout Equipment, Fully Adjustable & Lightweight Update 10/14/17
So yesterday I was riding my FitDesk when at about 8 minutes, I started to hear a soft clunking. It continued till I was finished. Today when I started pedaling, there was no noise, but after a few minutes the clunking started again, and it not only got a little louder, but I could feel the rubbing and clunking with each rotation; I found it distracting enough that I stopped earlier than I had planned. The pedals are nice and tight, and I haven't used this bike that much.

Update 04/19/17
The seat never felt that comfy, so I got the widest bike seat I could find - it's 13" wide, and that seems to work much better than the narrower seats, as my "sit bones" are over 10" apart.

Update 10/05/16
My husband cut down the saddle tube (part 66 in the manual) the seat sits on, cut two holes in the side for the pin to go through, and voila! The Fitdesk now fits me perfectly - and while I was concerned that sitting lower would make the desktop too high to use, it's actually more comfortable for me :) Next step will be to create a seat back that reclines!

Original review
There are a few things that stood out for me about the Fitdesk v2.0. First is the size of the cranks, 135mm, which is 35 to 40mm shorter than the cranks on most exercise bikes. Since I have short legs, the shorter (but not short) cranks were what first drew me to try the Fitdesk. I like the idea of being able to work while pedaling, but the second thing that stood out for me is Fitdesk's customer support. I emailed them tons of questions before buying; they answered every one quickly, politely and knowledgeably. They also read the questions on this listing, as I asked one and when no users responded, Fitdesk support did. I also like the configurableness (if that's even a word). If you want, you can get an adapter and use any bicycle seat on the Fitdesk; you can also get extenders to widen the desk section.

So I bought the Fitdesk, and pedaling is smooth and very quiet - quieter, actually, than my husband's Schwinn 170, which is a nice bike. It took my husband about 35 minutes to build my Fitdesk v2.0 (thanks, honey!), and when some missing parts were discovered, Fitdesk sent them to me and I had them in my hands in 4 days.

So why isn't this a 5 star review? First, this claim from the Fitdesk website - "Adjustable Lean. For a further "back lean" ride or a "forward lean" ride." Um, no. My Fitdesk's seat's furthest back lean is pretty much upright with just a hint of back lean; the other adjustments let you sit so your back is actually forward, which doesn't seem very useful to me. I would LOVE it if the seat had a couple adjustments allowing me to lean back further, and in fact that was one of the reasons I decided on the bike. Too bad it's not an accurate claim. I'd be one happy camper if I could adjust the seat back from upright to leaning back to leaning way back. Also the actual seat could be more comfortable, but everyone is different when it comes to seats. For now, it's more comfortable for me than most seats but after 30 minutes or so it gets just a little uncomfortable.

As a side note, my husband is a manufacturing engineer and CNC programmer, and he's considering whether he can make me a seat back holder that gives me the angles I want/need with the machines we have access to. In the meantime, the furthest back angle is good if you want to type.

Overall I like the Fitdesk quite a bit. The smooth, quiet action is very nice, the vulnerable parts of the body came wrapped so there's not a chip or scratch anywhere and Fitdesk support is really great. The desk itself is nicer in person than in pictures, and the rubber surface is just grippy enough; the desk fits my husband's 17" laptop well and my tablet very well. The computer's scan has a nice speed and seems very consistent. If only the seat back could be adjusted so it could either be used as it is now or lean back further, this would be a 5 star bike for me. As it is, the Fitdesk v2.0 is a very nice exercise bike and I'm really enjoying it.
text_fidelity_b: FitDesk Desk Bike 3.0 - Folding Exercise Bike for Work from Home Fitness, Stationary Bike and Desk Exercise Equipment with Built-in Tablet Holder, Bike Desk Workout Equipment, Fully Adjustable & Lightweight

Light and Motion Urban 800 FastCharge Bike Head Light It's a wonder I didn't get myself killed riding around with that AA powered headlight for so many years.

This isn't even the brightest model they make and it's almost as bright as a car's headlight. It illuminates the whole trail or street. The side lights illuminate your controls a bit and provide better visibility from the side. The light is a crisp, neutral white. Not yellow or cold blue.

It's actually too bright on full for the bike trail. Even the lowest setting is fine. I rode unlit bike trails at night for years with a light that wasn't half as bright on full as the L&M 800 is on its lowest setting.

Riding in fog? Yeah, this headlight is bright enough to make you visible.

Treat your headlight like your phone and charge it daily. The only thing missing from this headlight is a really accurate battery level indicator.

You may not want this headlight if you're doing six hour rides in the dead of night. Or if you're riding so far out in the boonies you're miles away from an electrical outlet. Most city and town riders will love this headlight, as will bike commuters.
text_fidelity_b: Light and Motion Urban 800 FastCharge Bike Head Light

It seems to be very well made but I wish it had some of the features of their other packs like the pockets on the waist strap or shoulder straps. It'd be nice to have my phone in front of me instead of in the pack itself but I guess that's what pockets are for. There are 2 stretchy water bottle pockets that seem to accommodate large bottles but they are hard to reach and impossible to put back without taking the pack off. At least that's what I've found out carrying a 1 liter sized bottle today.

The color is gorgeous! I love, love, LOVE it! It's a very deep aqua/turquoise color that's not overly bright or obnoxious. It's seriously one of the nicest looking packs I found in this price range when shopping and I looked at everyone and I mean EVERYONE! I spent about 2 days doing research and this was one of the best deals for the most volume out there. Overall, I think most students would be happy with it but it might be considered very large if you don't pack your books around all day. I carpool so I get dropped off at school in the morning and don't leave until early evening. I need to take all my books, workout clothes, food etc... So this pack still might be a little tight for all that but we'll see.

UPDATED 08/28/14

The bag has held up extremely well. I questioned how the elastic pockets on the front and sides would hold up and they seem to be just fine. After having it for a year I have to say the shape is frustrating. It's too tall and narrow so it wastes too much space. I find myself having to stack things on top of my books to take full advantage of the size of the bag. Other than that, it's been comfortable, kept my stuff dry on rainy days and still looks new! I'm glad I'm graduating in December because I'd probably want to buy another bag and I don't think my husband would appreciate that very much ;-)
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Unisex-Adult Daypack Backpacks
